passages.text: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a noninvasive method of imaging body structures based on the distribution of fixed water and other hydrogen-rich molecules in the human body. MRI uses a powerful magnet to align hydrogen atoms within the patient's soft tissues. As the nuclei return from excitation to equilibrium, the MRI receiver coil receives radio frequency wave signals that are transformed by the computer into diagnostic images. MRI produces cross sectional and 3-D images of soft tissues. Because bone contains little water (hydrogen nuclei), bone is relatively invisible to MRI. Blood is also relatively invisible because the hydrogen nuclei are moving in the blood stream.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: MRI contrast agents can improve the sensitivity and/or specificity of an image, by altering inherent tissue response to magnetic fields. The contrast agent most commonly used is gadolinium.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: MRI has proven useful in diagnosing cerebral infarctions, tumors, abscesses, edema, hemorrhage, nerve fiber demyelination (as in multiple sclerosis), and other disorders that increase fluid content of the affected tissues.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: MRI of the spinal canal has the advantage of noninvasive visualization of the spinal cord.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: MRI can:
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Differentiate solid from cystic tumors,
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Diagnose and localize spinal cord compression;
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Diagnose syringomyelia (progressive, chronic sensory disturbance, atrophy and spasticity of the spinal cord), disc disease, and any altered relationship between vertebral bodies, discs, spinal cord and nerve roots;
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Detect congenital spinal dysraphism (failure of fusion of parts along the dorsal midline of the spinal cord);
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Provide early detection of osteomyelitis, and
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Detect spinal cord abnormalities associated with osteomyelitis.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Coverage is limited to MRI units that have received FDA pre-market approval. Such units must be operated within the parameters specified by the approval.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Contrast is indicated for studying the central nervous system for metastatic disease, inflammatory disease, recurrent tumor versus scar, differentiation of microvascular from macrovascular infarction, and selected cases of complex vascular disease. Within the study of the spine, contrast also is indicated to differentiate recurrent disc versus scar or granulation tissue, spinal cord neoplasm, any case of myelopathy, and inflammatory cord disease.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: History and clinical findings are critical factors to determine when a lumbar MRI is needed in order to efficiently manage low back pain and related disorders.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Lumbar MRI may be indicated for a patient with a "red-flag" condition, such as a suspected tumor, infection, herniated intervertebral disc with nerve compression, or a major neurological problem. The MRI test result may be needed to evaluate these conditions to determine the need for surgery or other aggressive therapy, such as a work-up for metastatic cancer.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: "Red flags" are identified through an appropriate history plus a physical examination that typically includes evaluating muscle strength, limb circumference, reflexes, sensation, straight leg raise, and sitting knee extension tests.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: "Red flags" include:
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Major trauma
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Minor trauma in a potentially osteoporotic patient
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: History of cancer
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Fever
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Chills
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Unexplained weight loss
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Recent bacterial infection
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: IV drug abuse
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Immune suppression
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Pain that worsens when supine or at night
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Saddle anesthesia
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Recent onset of bladder dysfunction
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Clinically significant or progressive neurologic deficit in the lower extremity
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Unexpected laxity of the anal sphincter
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Perianal or perineal sensory loss,
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Clinically significant motor weakness, or
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Other nerve root compromise
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Eighty (80) to ninety (90) percent of patients with low back pain improve one month after symptom onset even without treatment. Therefore, spinal imaging tests are not generally necessary during the first month of symptoms except when a "red flag" (suggesting a medically emergent condition) is noted on the medical history and physical examination. For a "non-red flag" condition, the MRI may be appropriate after 1 month of symptoms.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: For example, for a patient with low back pain syndrome where there is no known injury, history of cancer, or septic disorder and there are no symptoms or signs suggesting nerve root disorder or spinal cord dysfunction (i.e. no "red flags"), MRI will be covered only if the patient has not responded to a reasonable trial of conservative management lasting at least four weeks.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: If a patient's limitations due to low back symptoms do not improve within four weeks, findings on reassessment may reveal an indication for a MRI. However, since MRI changes are common in asymptomatic patients, MRI abnormalities alone do not retrospectively validate the need for the test without other supporting clinical rationale.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: A lumbar MRI used to evaluate uncomplicated degenerative disc disease or herniated nucleus pulposus is not considered medically necessary when a surgical intervention or other aggressive treatment (e.g. intervertebral joint injection) is not under consideration.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: When a lumbar MRI is ordered, Medicare expects that the information gained from the test will be used for medical decision-making. When the findings will not affect the treatment choices, the test is not reasonable or necessary.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Certain uses of lumbar MRI are considered investigational and are therefore not covered by Medicare. These include the measurement of blood flow, spectroscopy, imaging of cortical bone and calcifications, and for procedures involving spatial resolution of bone or calcifications.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: A lumbar MRI that is a duplication of other imaging studies (such as a spinal CT scan) may be unreasonable or unnecessary. A lumbar MRI, however, could be complementary to a lumbar CT if there are inconclusive findings on a CT scan. Conversely, a lumbar CT may be warranted following an MRI study if the MRI study is found to be inconclusive. Documentation should support the medical necessity for the need for both studies.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: The payment for a single lumbar MRI procedure includes two (2) and three (3) sequences.
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Contraindications and limitations of lumbar MRI testing include:
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: Patients with an allergy to contrast media,
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: The effects upon a fetus are unknown at this time; therefore, pregnancy is to be handled at the discretion of the primary doctor,
passages.section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity

passages.text: When the technical component is performed without the professional component.
